rows.title: Open problem: Interfaces of the honeycomb O(n) loop model converge to SLE(kappa)
rows.body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For n in [0, 2] and x = 1/sqrt(2 + sqrt(2 - n)) the honeycomb O(n) loop-model interface converges to SLE(kappa) with kappa = 4 pi/(2 pi - arccos(-n/2)); for x above that value it converges to SLE(kappa) with kappa = 4 pi/arccos(-n/2). Known only for n = 1 at the critical point (site percolation, Smirnov) and for the n = 0 boundary in the trivial sense. Source: Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman, Slade: Lectures on self-avoiding walks, Clay 2012, Conjecture 3.7, p. 25. Status notes: The n = 0 critical case is the SLE(8/3) conjecture for SAW (the source's Conjecture 1.5), which the Codex campaign already records as P0003 (hexagonal SAW scaling limit); this record covers n in (0,2] and the dense phase, and the n = 0 dense case (x above critical, kappa = 8).
Posed in Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman, Slade: Lectures on self-avoiding walks, Clay 2012
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

rows.title: Attempt on Interfaces of the honeycomb O(n) loop model converge to SLE(kappa)
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check which n have any discrete holomorphic observable and which have crossing estimates. Result: Duminil-Copin-Smirnov's parafermionic observable exists for all n in [0,2] at the critical x with spin sigma = 1 - 3 arccos(-n/2)/(4 pi)... (the spin depends on n) and satisfies the contour relations; full holomorphicity holds for none except the Ising-related n = 1 dilute? (n = 1 corresponds to the Ising model's low-temperature expansion on the honeycomb, for which the observable is the Ising fermion and IS holomorphic — that is how Smirnov's Ising result and Chelkak-Smirnov work; on the honeycomb the n = 1 loop model at x_c is the critical Ising model, so the n = 1 case at the critical point IS known via Ising, contrary to the naive reading; the source's remark 'n = 1 site percolation' refers to the dense phase x = 1, kappa = 6). So: n = 1 critical (Ising, SLE(3)) and n = 1 dense (percolation, SLE(6)) are both known; n = 2 corresponds to kappa = 4 (GFF level lines) and is open; n in (0,1) union (1,2) open in both phases; n = 0 critical open (P0003), n = 0 dense (kappa = 8, uniform spanning tree-like, x = 1: the dense O(0) model at x = 1 is the Hamiltonian-cycle-type model... open). RSW-type crossing estimates for the O(n) model are known for n in [1,2] (Duminil-Copin-Glazman-Peled-Spinka, 2020) giving tightness of interfaces; identification of the limit needs the holomorphicity, which only n = 1 has. Rigorous partial: the conjecture at n = 1 is a theorem in both phases; for n in (1,2] tightness holds and only identification is missing; for n in [0,1) even tightness (crossing estimates) is missing. Key identity: n = 1 critical honeycomb O(n) = critical Ising (holomorphic fermion, SLE(3) proved); n = 1 dense = site percolation (SLE(6) proved). Obstruction: Holomorphicity fails for n not 1; crossing estimates unavailable for n < 1.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0096-interfaces-of-the-honeycomb-o-n-loop-model-converge-to-sle-kappa
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved
